rounds.title: Swift foundations and ownership
rounds.brief: Explain syntax and semantics clearly before introducing production architecture.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to establish the scenario, owners and assumptions before timed questions.
Answer the six prompts without revealing model answers; ask for missing assumptions.
Use the remaining time to change one input and debrief the mistaken predictions. Reserve 6 debrief minutes for evidence gaps and the next retrieval task.
evidence: Correct assignment and optional/error distinctions.
An ownership graph rather than only weak-self vocabulary.
One runnable or clearly labeled predicted example, plus a next retrieval task.

rounds.title: UI implementation and lifecycle review
rounds.brief: Defend a screen under changing content, ownership and layout conditions.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to establish the scenario, owners and assumptions before timed questions.
Discuss lifecycle, stable identity, layout and editing using the selected prompts.
Finish with large-text, RTL, keyboard, reuse and interrupted-navigation evidence. Reserve 8 debrief minutes for evidence gaps and the next retrieval task.
evidence: No conflation of SwiftUI identity and UIKit controller lifetime.
A stable-item and obsolete-result policy.
Specific device/interaction gaps and a bounded verification matrix.

rounds.title: Concurrency, streams and account-scoped data
rounds.brief: Reason about asynchronous interleavings instead of reciting API names.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to establish the scenario, owners and assumptions before timed questions.
Answer each prompt with a controlled completion ordering.
Debrief cancellation, error preservation and A-to-B-to-A account transitions. Reserve 9 debrief minutes for evidence gaps and the next retrieval task.
evidence: Distinguishes suspension, isolation, reentrancy and background work.
A precise buffer, cancellation and shared-operation contract.
Deterministic fake gates and separate cache versus UI publication checks.

rounds.title: Performance investigation and optimization defense
rounds.brief: Propose an optimization only after establishing correctness and a measurement contract.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to establish the scenario, owners and assumptions before timed questions.
Trace startup, frame, memory and resource hypotheses with the selected prompts.
Conclude with raw evidence requirements, regression gates and residual uncertainty. Reserve 10 debrief minutes for evidence gaps and the next retrieval task.
evidence: No invented p95, energy gain or physical-device result.
Separates mechanism evidence from outcome measurements.
Tradeoffs preserve product behavior and identify conditions that reverse the recommendation.

rounds.title: Build variants, libraries and delivery contracts
rounds.brief: Explain the installed artifact and its dependency/resource graph.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to establish the scenario, owners and assumptions before timed questions.
Review dependency, generated code, resources and verification coordinates.
Rehearse reconstruction and installed-client recovery without performing a release. Reserve 9 debrief minutes for evidence gaps and the next retrieval task.
evidence: Package/product/target/import and requirement/pin distinctions.
Effective setting and target-membership evidence.
A narrow verification matrix and an honest recovery boundary.

rounds.title: Platform services and cross-process boundaries
rounds.brief: Keep trust, permission, scene, process and durable-state ownership explicit.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to establish the scenario, owners and assumptions before timed questions.
Release delayed events after changing account, document, scene or process conditions.
Debrief device, signing, interprocess and protected-data checks that remain pending. Reserve 9 debrief minutes for evidence gaps and the next retrieval task.
evidence: No promise of exact background or widget scheduling.
Typed failure and stale-owner handling at the final transaction.
Distinct source, fake, device and distribution evidence.

rounds.title: Staff-level design, migration and influence
rounds.brief: Practice an architectural decision under constraints, not a memorized system-design script.
steps: Use 10 setup minutes to define users, constraints, success criteria and decision ownership.
Compare at least two alternatives and an incremental compatibility seam.
Address measurement, privacy, rollout, recovery and cross-team verification.
Use the debrief to state what evidence would reverse the recommendation. Reserve 10 debrief minutes for evidence gaps and the next retrieval task.
evidence: A bounded proposal with alternatives and measurable acceptance.
Explicit risk owners, compatibility stages and recovery constraints.
Reproducible reviewer evidence and communication, not a claim that a score confers staff readiness.

rounds.title: Android-to-iOS engineering handoff
rounds.brief: Share a product contract across platforms without pretending their implementations are identical.
steps: Use 6 setup minutes to establish the scenario, owners and assumptions before timed questions.
Translate one Android assumption and demonstrate where it fails on iOS.
Finish with a reviewable implementation/verification handoff and residual specialist gaps. Reserve 10 debrief minutes for evidence gaps and the next retrieval task.
evidence: Precise Kotlin/Java analogy boundaries.
Independent lifecycle, executor, resource and platform-availability reasoning.
An actionable evidence ledger that another engineer could reproduce.

rounds.title: Beginner Swift: first program, values, functions and collections
rounds.brief: Explain a small synthetic Swift program and predict its behavior before running it.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to choose a synthetic input, establish tool/language boundaries and state the expected output.
Use the four authored question budgets (26 minutes total). Keep 4 minutes for changed-input clarification; do not borrow from the debrief.
Reserve 10 debrief minutes to compare prediction with available host evidence and choose one syntax or collection retrieval task.
evidence: Explains program entry and tools without treating a host executable as an iOS app.
Predicts value, function-label and collection behavior with explicit input/output.
Records observed versus predicted results and one concrete correction, without automatic completion.

rounds.title: Beginner SwiftUI: first app, composition, state and navigation
rounds.brief: Trace a small scratch screen from state ownership through rendering and a navigation action.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to name the scratch target, screen state owner and expected interaction.
Use the four authored question budgets (29 minutes total). Keep 1 minute for clarification; deeper state/navigation follow-ups belong in a separate block.
Reserve 10 debrief minutes for actual versus predicted UI evidence, build/runtime limits and the next bounded scratch task.
evidence: Distinguishes first app setup, view values and native runtime verification.
Explains modifier composition and the source of truth for state/bindings.
Routes using stable owned state and leaves unexecuted device/accessibility checks pending.

rounds.title: Principal cross-team strategy: platform contract, adoption and retirement
rounds.brief: Own a synthetic cross-team platform decision with native execution boundaries, cost, accountable owners, adoption evidence and installed-client recovery.
steps: Use 10 setup minutes to define the shared product contract, affected teams, installed-client constraints and decision owner.

Use the 88 authored question minutes to compare local adapters, a shared behavior contract and a shared execution engine; connect each selected prompt to cost, owners, adoption and platform boundaries.
Name pilot gates, consumer exceptions, stop authority and adoption/outcome/cost denominators; rehearse future-operation rollback and pre-configuration failure without replaying ambiguous writes.
Reserve 12 debrief minutes to critique evidence, successful old-path retirement versus candidate removal on rejection, and conditions that reverse the decision.
evidence: Separates the staff implementation seam from principal funding, sequencing and cross-team accountability.
Compares viable options with explicit estimates, opportunity cost and named proposed owners.
Defines measurable adoption with exceptions and compatible installed-client recovery.
Uses retirement criteria and an accountable debt owner; no title or production outcome is inferred from the exercise.

rounds.title: Runtime, scheduling and synchronization
rounds.brief: Explain event eligibility and ownership, then diagnose a blocked or canceled workload without assuming a task owns a thread.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to state the scenario, environment, owners and missing assumptions.
Answer the three prompts within their individual timeboxes without model answers; use remaining rehearsal time for a changed input or adverse ordering.
Reserve 15 debrief minutes to identify unsupported claims, revise one decision and record the next independent exercise or evidence request.
evidence: A traced RunLoop or queue contract and the current mode or owner.
A cancellation/completion policy that survives an adverse ordering.
A bounded worker intervention with the proposed and observed effects distinguished.

rounds.title: Swift migration and transfer boundaries
rounds.brief: Read effective compiler settings before changing annotations; preserve state transfer, clock and cancellation contracts.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to state the scenario, environment, owners and missing assumptions.
Answer the three prompts within their individual timeboxes without model answers; use remaining rehearsal time for a changed input or adverse ordering.
Reserve 15 debrief minutes to identify unsupported claims, revise one decision and record the next independent exercise or evidence request.
evidence: The compiler/language/isolation matrix and a reproduced diagnostic.
A justification for transfer versus shared ownership, including the legacy boundary.
A deterministic context, clock or channel schedule and its teardown behavior.

rounds.title: UI runtime and independent scene lifetimes
rounds.brief: Trace event routing and cache validity, then revise a lifecycle assumption involving reconnecting or interrupted UI.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to state the scenario, environment, owners and missing assumptions.
Answer the three prompts within their individual timeboxes without model answers; use remaining rehearsal time for a changed input or adverse ordering.
Reserve 15 debrief minutes to identify unsupported claims, revise one decision and record the next independent exercise or evidence request.
evidence: A responder/observation owner and a precise teardown path.
A layout input/invalidation contract with a changed width, direction or text case.
A process/scene/view distinction and a durable restoration policy.

rounds.title: Durable upgrade, replay and account recovery
rounds.brief: Defend an upgrade and replay design when the process exits, server outcome is ambiguous or the account changes before commit.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to state the scenario, environment, owners and missing assumptions.
Answer the three prompts within their individual timeboxes without model answers; use remaining rehearsal time for a changed input or adverse ordering.
Reserve 15 debrief minutes to identify unsupported claims, revise one decision and record the next independent exercise or evidence request.
evidence: Actual old-store preservation evidence or a clearly pending Apple-store check.
A persisted command identity and server reconciliation/idempotency requirement.
An account and storage-failure recovery path without silent deletion or duplicate effects.

rounds.title: Profiling evidence and regression decisions
rounds.brief: Separate authored instrumentation from a recorded trace, explain an intervention and reject incompatible raw observations.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to state the scenario, environment, owners and missing assumptions.
Answer the three prompts within their individual timeboxes without model answers; use remaining rehearsal time for a changed input or adverse ordering.
Reserve 15 debrief minutes to identify unsupported claims, revise one decision and record the next independent exercise or evidence request.
evidence: Matching environment, workload and phase boundaries.
A retained trace/interval or an explicitly pending capture.
Correctness, raw attempted outcomes and a predeclared acceptance decision.

rounds.title: Artifact identity, staff review and principal adoption
rounds.brief: Join product identity and independent critique to an adoption decision, then change a recovery or team constraint.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to state the scenario, environment, owners and missing assumptions.
Answer the three prompts within their individual timeboxes without model answers; use remaining rehearsal time for a changed input or adverse ordering.
Reserve 15 debrief minutes to identify unsupported claims, revise one decision and record the next independent exercise or evidence request.
evidence: A reviewable artifact/configuration identity with missing evidence visible.
An original critique, revised implementation decision and affected recheck.
Owned adoption/exception/retirement gates and a viable no-change alternative.

rounds.title: Apple capability selection and unsupported states
rounds.brief: Choose a capability from product needs, state its real trust/lifecycle/conflict contract and bound the next specialist exercise.
steps: Use 5 setup minutes to state the scenario, environment, owners and missing assumptions.
Answer the three prompts within their individual timeboxes without model answers; use remaining rehearsal time for a changed input or adverse ordering.
Reserve 15 debrief minutes to identify unsupported claims, revise one decision and record the next independent exercise or evidence request.
evidence: A justified feature selection with a simpler viable alternative.
A verified or synthetic policy outcome labeled with its actual evidence kind.
Unsupported states, account/consent constraints and a concrete specialist follow-up.
